input.question: Do the pre-2024 and post-2024 versions of Regulation 16(1)(c) permit the same scope of borrowing by Category I AIFs?

response.answer:
The pre-2024 version of Regulation 16(1)(c) permits Category I Alternative Investment Funds to borrow funds only to meet temporary funding requirements for not more than thirty days, on not more than four occasions in a year, and not more than ten percent of the investable funds.

The post-2024 version of Regulation 16(1)(c), effective from 07-08-2024, permits borrowing for temporary funding requirements as well as day-to-day operational requirements, with the same limits of not more than thirty days, on not more than four occasions in a year, and not more than ten percent of the investable funds.

Therefore, the scope of borrowing is broader after 2024 as it explicitly includes day-to-day operational requirements in addition to temporary funding, unlike the pre-2024 regulation which only explicitly allowed temporary funding borrowing.

input.question: Do the original definition of 'representative' and the 2020-amended definition of 'persons associated with investment advice' cover the same set of persons within an investment advisory firm?

response.answer:
The original definition of 'representative' referred only to employees or agents of an investment adviser who render investment advice on behalf of the adviser.

The 2020-amended definition of 'persons associated with investment advice' includes a broader group such as members, partners, officers, directors, employees, sales staff, and similar client-facing persons engaged in providing advisory services, but excludes clerical or administrative staff without client interface.

Therefore, the 2020 definition covers a wider and more inclusive set of persons associated with investment advice compared to the original definition of 'representative'.

citations.quote:

Regulation 2(1)(r) (original, pre-2020): 'representative' means an employee or an agent of an investment adviser who renders investment advice on behalf of that investment adviser.

Passage B:
Regulation 2(1)(r) (as substituted w.e.f. 30-09-2020): 'persons associated with investment advice' shall mean any member, partner, officer, director or employee or any sales staff of such investment adviser including any person occupying a similar status or performing a similar function irrespective of the nature of association with the investment adviser who is engaged in providing investment advisory services to the clients of the investment adviser. Explanation — All client-facing persons such as sales staff, service relationship managers, client relationship managers, etc., by whatever name called shall be deemed to be persons associated with investment advice, but do not include persons who discharge clerical or office administrative functions where there is no client interface.

input.question: May an agent move a payment that is already scheduled to a different date?

response.answer:
An agent may not move, amend, or cancel a payment that is already scheduled through servicing tooling, nor move an existing instalment to a different date by scheduling another payment, as this creates a second obligation.

If a customer requests to change the date of a scheduled payment, the agent must verify the customer, clearly inform them that the date cannot be changed automatically, and escalate the case to a human agent.

citations.quote:
## Payments

An agent may schedule a **new** one-off payment against an active loan: due no earlier than today
and no more than **60 days** ahead, for an amount between **₹100** and **₹5,00,000**. A loan that
has been closed takes no further payments.

The servicing tooling cannot move, amend or cancel a payment that is already scheduled, and
scheduling a second payment does not replace the first — it creates a second obligation, and the
customer will be collected for both. So a request to *move* an existing instalment to a different
date is not something an agent may do by scheduling another payment. Verify the customer, tell
them plainly that the date cannot be changed automatically, and hand the case to a human. A
request to add a payment the customer does not already owe — a part payment, an extra payment —
is an ordinary scheduling request and needs no escalation.
citations.title: Harbour servicing policy (internal)

citations.quote:
## Identity before money

No agent may move money, change a payment obligation, or forgive a charge until the customer's
identity has been verified on the current contact. This applies to scheduling a payment, cancelling
an auto-debit mandate, waiving a fee, and applying a hardship plan. It applies even when the
customer is plainly who they say they are, even when they have called before, and even when they
are impatient.

Verification means confirming the last four digits of the registered mobile number against the
account record. A verification that has been recorded on this contact is good for the remainder of
the contact and no longer.

If verification fails, say so plainly, do not hint at the correct answer, and do not offer a second
route to the same outcome. Two failed attempts on one contact end the automated journey: hand the
case to a human. A customer who cannot verify may still be given general information that is not
account-specific, and may still be told how to verify through the app.

Reading a loan record, looking at payment history, requesting a document, sending a statement to
the address already on file, and escalating are not money movements and do not require prior
verification. Sending a statement anywhere other than the address already on the record is not
permitted at all; the contact record must be updated first, through the normal contact-change
route.

input.question: Do the original and 2018-amended versions of Regulation 16(3) provide the same grounds for a credit rating agency to withdraw a rating of an outstanding security?

response.answer:
The original Regulation 16(3) allowed a credit rating agency to withdraw a rating only if the company whose security is rated is wound up or merged or amalgamated with another company while the security obligations are outstanding.

The 2018-amended Regulation 16(3) added an additional exception allowing withdrawal of a rating also as may be specified by the Board from time to time, in addition to the original grounds of winding up or merger/amalgamation of the company.

Passage B:
Regulation 16(3) (as substituted w.e.f. 30-05-2018): A credit rating agency shall not withdraw a rating so long as the obligations under the security rated by it are outstanding, except where the company whose security is rated is wound up or merged or amalgamated with another company, or as may be specified by the Board from time to time.

input.question: How much advance notice must SEBI give to an investment adviser before ordering an inspection under SEBI IA Regulations, 2013? Under what circumstances can SEBI dispense with this notice?

response.answer:
SEBI must give not less than ten days notice to the investment adviser before ordering an inspection under SEBI IA Regulations, 2013.

SEBI can dispense with this ten days notice if it is satisfied that in the interest of the investors no such notice should be given, and in such cases may order inspection without notice by an order in writing.
